newsitem.title: INDIA: India BSE plans to start share depository by April.
newsitem.headline: India BSE plans to start share depository by April.

text.p: India's premier bourse, the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), expects to start a share depository by April this year, its chief said on Thursday.
"India Securities Depository Ltd is expected to start working by April 1997," BSE president Madan Gopal Damani said at a news conference.
The depository immobilises share certificates, eliminates cumbersome physical transfer of shares whenever these are bought or sold and ushers in paperless trading.
India's first share depository was launched in November by the rival National Stock Exchange which operates from 53 centres across the country.
Damani said he had suggested a number of measures for reviving the sagging capital markets at a meeting between Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda and industrialists and economists on Tuesday.
These included the removal of a controversial minimum tax on companies and tax-breaks on company dividends.
Damani said he was hopeful that the government would accept his suggestions and announce new measures before the 1997/98 (April-March) budget due at the end of February.
The BSE chief said he has been invited by finance minister P. Chidambaram to discuss ways to revive the markets at a meeting scheduled on January 11.
The benchmark BSE index on Thursday closed 35.32 points, or 1.08 percent, lower at 3,225.24 -- after vaulting 175.36 points, or 5.68 percent, on Wednesday.
